goal: `mc shot dev|prod <target>` gives back a PNG of the running app, a local dev server or https://meetmemoro.app. The picture can be the whole page, one element picked by `--el <css>`, or one shell picked by `--shell base|immersive|window`, and the command prints the file's path. It signs in as the seeded test account by default. On production, `--me` signs in as Martin, from a session he gave mc once with `mc shot login prod`. Martin, 2026-09-26: "smidiga smarta sätt att generera screenshots från dev-server eller live prod … antingen av enskilda element eller av sidor (base shell eller window shell)". Asked which account production uses, he answered: "Båda, testkonto som standard".

mc owns the environment: which worktree, which server (started the way `mc test dev` starts one), the base URL, the token and the session in the keychain, and where the file goes. memoro owns the app: `.mc/shot.json` and the capture script it names, built by the memoro project `shot-capture` (`docs/project/test-architecture/shot-capture/PLAN.json` in memoro). The two sides meet only through the request file and the result line below. The memoro plan carries the same text word for word.
contract: **The interface to mc, fixed.** mc runs `.mc/shot.json`'s `argv` with `cwd` set to the memoro worktree and `MEMORO_SHOT_REQUEST=<absolute path to a JSON file>` in the environment. That file is mode 0600, mc deletes it afterwards, and it is the only place a token or cookie ever appears. The script must never print the file's contents, the token or the cookie, except the `session` field in login mode. The request has this shape: `{ "mode": "capture" | "login", "base_url": "http://127.0.0.1:8787", "account": "seeded" | "me", "sign_in": { "kind": "url", "url": "…" } | { "kind": "session", "cookie": "<memoro_session value>" }, "target": { "name": "home" } | { "path": "/app/people" }, "element": "<css>" | null, "shell": "base" | "immersive" | "window" | null, "full_page": false, "viewport": "desktop" | { "width": 390, "height": 844, "dpr": 3, "mobile": true }, "theme": "light" | "dark" | null, "locale": "sv-SE" | null, "out": "/abs/file.png", "profile_dir": "/abs/dir" }`. `sign_in`, `target` and `out` are for capture only, and `profile_dir` for login only.

**The result line, fixed.** The script's last non-empty stdout line is one JSON object, and everything else it prints goes to stderr. A capture writes `{ "ok": true, "file": "/abs/file.png", "url": "<page URL, with any /demo/<token> redacted>", "subject": "page" | "element" | "shell", "selector": "<css or null>", "width": <px>, "height": <px>, "warnings": ["…"] }`. A login writes `{ "ok": true, "session": "<memoro_session cookie value>" }`. A failure writes `{ "ok": false, "code": "bad-request" | "not-signed-in" | "no-target" | "no-element" | "timeout" | "browser", "error": "<one sentence a person can act on>" }` and exits 1.
**A secret appears only in the request file and in the keychain.** The token, the `/demo/<token>` URL and the session cookie never appear in argv, stdout, stderr, `--json`, a log line or a file name.
**`mc test` does not change behaviour.** The step may extract a shared helper from `src/mc/commands/test.js`, but every existing test stays green unchanged.
out_of_scope: The capture script, the targets and the selectors are memoro's `shot-capture` project.
Visual diffing, batch capture of every target, and sending the file anywhere but the local disk (`--open` opens it locally, and that is all).
A `--me` on a dev server. Local servers have only the three managed accounts `/dev/login` offers (`src/routes/dev-login.js:90-102` in memoro).

success_criteria.criterion: `mc shot dev home`, `mc shot dev home --shell base`, `mc shot dev notifications --shell window` and `mc shot dev /app/people --el '.base-view__header'` each print the path of a PNG that shows what it names.
success_criteria.check: Once memoro's `shot-capture` has landed: run the four commands and open the four files. The step session checks the same paths against a fake capture script in the tests (see the step). A person checks the running app.

success_criteria.criterion: `mc shot prod home --viewport iphone` works on the test token alone. `mc shot prod home --me` works after one `mc shot login prod`, or after `mc shot login prod --paste` if Google refuses the automated browser.
success_criteria.check: Run it on this machine and look at the pictures. `mc shot prod home --me` without a stored session says `mc shot login prod` in one line and exits 1.

A test runs a fake capture script that dumps its argv and environment. The token and the cookie are found only in the request file, which is mode 0600 and gone afterwards, and never in mc's stdout or stderr.

documents.label: The memoro half: `.mc/shot.json` and the capture script
How `mc test dev|prod` reaches a server and the test account

steps.title: The `mc shot` verb
steps.done_when: `mc shot` is routed, has `--help` and a section in `mc help`, builds the request and runs memoro's declared capture script with the dev, prod and `--me` sign-ins, stores and forgets the session with `mc shot login|logout prod`, and is tested against a fake capture script; docs/technical/mc-shot.md, the changelog entry and the project_log row are in the same pull request.
instruction: **The verb's surface.** It has four forms. `mc shot <dev|prod> <target> [--el <css>] [--shell base|immersive|window] [--full] [--viewport <name|WxH[@dpr]>] [--theme light|dark] [--locale <code>] [--me] [--here] [--out <file.png>] [--open] [--json]` takes the picture. `mc shot <dev|prod> --list` prints the targets and viewports `.mc/shot.json` declares. `mc shot login prod [--paste]` stores Martin's session, and `mc shot logout prod` forgets it. The target is either a path starting with `/app`, or a target name from `.mc/shot.json` `targets[].name`; an unknown name gets an error that lists the known names. `--me` is refused on `dev`, `--here` is refused on `prod`, and `login` and `logout` exist only for `prod`, each refusal in one line. A viewport given as `WxH[@dpr]` becomes `{ width, height, dpr }` (default dpr 2, `mobile: true` when W < 600). A named viewport must be in `viewports`. Parse with `scanArgs` (`src/mc/commands/flags.js:22-58`), using `strictValues` for `--el --shell --viewport --theme --locale --out`.

**Where the verb goes.** Create `src/mc/commands/shot.js`, exporting `run(argv, deps = {})` and `usage()`, with `src/mc/commands/gate.js` as the model: deps for stdout, stderr, env, cwd, spawn, now. Register it as `shot` in `VERB_MODULES` (`src/mc-verbs.js:10-28`), and put it in `HELP_TEXT`, both in the quick list and under IN FULL (`src/mc/help-text.js`). `tests/mc/help.test.js` fails for a routed verb missing from the help, and `usage()` must start with `usage`. The logic goes in `src/mc/shot.js`: `readShotDeclaration(worktree)`, `parseViewport`, `outPath`, `buildRequest`, `parseResult`, `runCapture`.

**Worktree and base URL, as `mc test` finds them.** For the worktree, `--here` uses `callerWorktree(cwd)` and anything else uses `sharedWorktree(env)` (`src/mc/test-environment.js:115-141`). Read `.mc/shot.json` from it (a missing file gives the error `memoro has no .mc/shot.json at <worktree> — it comes with memoro's shot-capture project`) and `.mc/test.json` through `readDeclaration`. For prod, the base URL is `declaration.environments.prod.base_url`. For dev, extract the app-tier block of `environment()` in `src/mc/commands/test.js` (around :193-219: `ensureDevServer`, the progress lines, `baseUrl = String(server.url).replace(/\/+$/u, '')`) into one function that both verbs call. Pass `--json` through so that the progress lines stay off stdout. The static tier is not needed.

**Sign-in, by case.** On dev, it is `{ kind: 'url', url: `${base}/dev/login?account=seeded&ready=1` }` with account `seeded`. memoro's `/dev/login` exists only under `DEV_MODE` and, with `ready=1`, takes the account past onboarding (`src/routes/dev-login.js:104`, `:134-139` in memoro). mc has never built this URL itself; the suites did. On prod without `--me`, it is `tokenFor(declaration, env)` (`src/mc/test-environment.js:588`), then `{ kind: 'url', url: `${base}${account.route || '/demo/'}${token}` }` with account `seeded`. With no token, the error is `no test-account token — printf %s <token> | mc test token --set`, exit 1. On prod with `--me`, it is `getSecret('MEMORO_SHOT_SESSION')` from `src/lib/keychain.js:38`, then `{ kind: 'session', cookie }` with account `me`. With nothing stored, the error is `no session of yours is stored — mc shot login prod`, exit 1.

**The request and the run.** Write the request to `<mkdtemp(os.tmpdir(), 'mc-shot-')>/request.json` with mode 0600, and remove that directory in a `finally`. Spawn `.mc/shot.json` `argv` with `spawnSync` (or the async form with deps.spawn), `cwd: worktree`, `env: { ...env, MEMORO_SHOT_REQUEST: file }`, `stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'inherit']` so the script's progress reaches the terminal, and a 180 s timeout. Parse the last non-empty stdout line as JSON. A line that does not parse, a timeout, or a non-zero exit with no result line is an error that quotes the script's exit code. For `ok: false`, print `mc: <error>` and exit 1; when the code is `not-signed-in` and the account is `me`, also print `mc shot login prod`. For `ok: true`, print the file path alone on the first line (the path is the answer, and a caller can `$(mc shot … | head -1)`), then `url`, and each warning as `mc: warning — …`. `--json` prints the result object. `--open` runs `openCommandFor` from `src/lib/device-flow.js:168` on the file, detached with `stdio: 'ignore'`.

**Where the file goes.** `--out` is resolved against cwd; it must end `.png`, and its directory is created. Without `--out` the file goes to `join(mcHome(), 'shots', name)` (`src/mc/paths.js:21`), where `name` is `<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>-<dev|prod>[-me]-<target>[-<shell>|-el]-<viewport>[-<theme>].png`. `<target>` is the target name, or the path slugified (`/app/people` → `app-people`, `/app/` → `app`). `<viewport>` is the name or `WxH`. Local time is used, as `ls` shows it.

**`mc shot login prod`.** Without `--paste`, it builds a request `{ mode: 'login', base_url, profile_dir: join(mcHome(), 'shots', '.chrome-profile-prod') }`, runs it as above, and on `ok: true` calls `setSecret('MEMORO_SHOT_SESSION', result.session)`. It prints `mc: your session is stored — mc shot prod <target> --me` and never the value. On `timeout`, the script's error already names `--paste`; print it. With `--paste`, it reads stdin, trims it, strips a leading `memoro_session=`, and refuses an empty value. It stores the value, then says so. The value is the `memoro_session` cookie from meetmemoro.app, copied from Chrome's DevTools → Application → Cookies; the usage text says where to find it. `mc shot logout prod` calls `deleteSecret('MEMORO_SHOT_SESSION')`. The session is valid for 90 days of disuse (`src/auth/session-cookie.js:5` in memoro). mc does not check it at store time: the next `--me` shot reports `not-signed-in` if it is wrong.

**Tests** in `tests/mc/shot.test.js` (`node:test`, deps injected, and `tests/_isolate-home.mjs` already sets `MC_HOME`). Cover: flag parsing and each refusal; target resolution and the unknown-name error, against a fixture `.mc/shot.json` in a temp worktree; `parseViewport`; `outPath`; each of the three sign-in cases with a stubbed `tokenFor` or keychain; `--list`. For the run, use a fixture capture script (`argv: [process.execPath, '<fixture>.mjs']`) that writes a small PNG to `request.out`, copies its request, argv and env to a side file, and prints the result line. From that side file, assert that the token, the demo URL and the cookie appear nowhere except in the request, that the request file was mode 0600 and is gone afterwards, and that mc's stdout and stderr do not contain them either. Also cover a script printing `ok: false` with `not-signed-in` for `me`, and a script printing garbage. Do not start a browser or a real dev server in the tests. Run `npm test` and land with `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`.

**Docs in the same pull request.** `docs/technical/mc-shot.md` describes what exists: the forms, the interface to memoro (point to `.mc/shot.json` in memoro rather than copying the targets), the keychain name, the output directory, and what `--me` can and cannot do. Add a row for `mc shot` to `docs/mc-command-matrix.md`. Add `changelog.d/mc-shot.md` with `section: Added`. Add a row to `docs/project/project_log.md` for this project. If memoro's `shot-capture` has landed by the time you finish (`git show origin/main:.mc/shot.json` in `~/memoro`), run the first criterion's four commands against a dev server, look at the pictures, and mark `met`. Otherwise leave it unmarked and say so in a comment on the step.
